A quote-blind `split("#", 1)[0]` stripper yields an identical site set and identical bound flags across all six wrappers, and `_LIVE` passes identically both ways — so the round-3 rationale ("every watch push line carries a `#` a naive strip would cut into") was false, and the control billed as the over-strip guard controlled nothing.

The code is kept, because a real shape does need it: a `#` inside a quoted argument BEFORE the push variable. `_LIVE_HASH_BEFORE_SITE` builds that from two ADJACENT live lines of `cron_watch_issue_2091.sh` — the `echo "$(ts) #${ISSUE} ..."` log line at 51 and the retirement push at 52 — fused with `&&` onto one physical line, the wrappers' own logging idiom.

Two changes, not one: (1) the stated rationale in `_strip_bash_comment` and in the `_LIVE` block comment is corrected to that shape, and scoped honestly (the trailing-message hash is INERT); (2) `test_quote_tracking_is_load_bearing_when_a_hash_precedes_the_site` RUNS the naive strip rather than asserting about it — quote-aware gives one bounded site, quote-blind gives zero. Verified failing under truncation before it was committed. `test_quote_blind_stripping_is_indistinguishable_on_the_live_line` pins the corrected scope so the false claim cannot return.

CLOSED at f16c71b301b by context tracking, not retreat. `)` REMAINS in
`_COMMENT_WORD_START` — removing it would reopen the round-3 silent channel
(`cron_watch_issue_2091.sh:50` is a real `archived)` case arm dispatching the
terminal push at `:52`). Instead `_strip_bash_comment`'s character walk now
carries `open_parens: list[bool]`, `last_substitution_close` and `prev_bare`
(previous unquoted, unescaped char): a `(` pushes True when preceded by `$`,
`<` or `>`; `$((` pushes two and consumes both; a `)` popping True records its
index and the `#` test skips it. Subshell `)`, `case`-arm `)` and a bare `((`
arithmetic command's `))` all still end a word.
